back: Usually interchangeable for obligations/recommendations; 'should' is more frequent [13].
Used when evidence suggests something is certain or very likely [13].
Prefer 'should' when stating what an outside authority recommends (e.g., 'The manual says...') [13].
Use 'should' (or 'would') (e.g., 'I should leave early if I were you') [13].
Use 'should/ought to have + past participle' for things that DIDN'T happen [13].
Use 'should/ought to have + past participle' to say something happened or will have happened [13].
Use 'should' in questions (e.g., 'Should I phone for a taxi?') [13].
Used to say a particular action is a good idea now (esp. in spoken English) [13].
Used for urgency, demands, or threats (e.g., 'We'd better call the police') [13].
